parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain what is meant by a ‘matched pairs design’.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Explain one advantage of using a matched pairs design compared to using a repeated
measures design.

text: A matched pairs design is an experimental design that can be used in studies comparing two
conditions, or levels, of an independent variable.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Define the term ‘range’.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Describe how the range of ‘hours spent asleep’ could have been calculated in the study by
Dement and Kleitman (sleep and dreams).

text: A range can be calculated when numerical scores are collected from participants in a study.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
One way to check reliability is the test-retest technique.
Describe how this technique checks reliability.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Another type of reliability is inter-rater reliability.
Explain how the inter-rater reliability of studies can be improved.

text: The reliability of a study is affected by the measures (scales or tasks) chosen by the researcher
and the way that these are used when conducting the study.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Explain what is meant by the term ‘conclusions’, using an example from a core study from the
social approach.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
In the study by Baron-Cohen et al. (eyes test), two main conclusions were drawn.
Outline one of these conclusions.

text: In each of the core studies, the researchers report their conclusions.
In the study by Saavedra and Silverman (button phobia), a boy was repeatedly asked to use
the Feelings Thermometer. Other questions investigated his phobia further and showed that he
disliked buttons touching his body.
Explain the type of interview used in this study.
Describe the ethical guidelines of ‘housing’ and ‘rewards’ in relation to animals, using any
examples.

Section B
Answer all questions in this section.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain why Dr Casson’s study was a field experiment.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: Suggest how Dr Casson could have measured the dependent variable in her study.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
Suggest one reason why it may be more difficult to measure the dependent variable in a
field experiment than in a laboratory experiment.

text: Dr Casson conducted a field experiment to compare the emotions that people show when they
respond to shop assistants who are either wearing a uniform or casual clothes. She asked the
assistants at her local shop to wear a uniform on Saturdays and wear casual clothes on Sundays.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Suggest how Keung and Jovita could measure the physical activity level of their participants.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Write a null hypothesis for Keung and Jovita’s correlational study.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Keung predicted that there would be a positive correlation and Jovita predicted that there
would be a negative correlation.
Their results show that a higher physical activity level is related to a lower attention level.
Explain whether Keung or Jovita’s prediction was correct.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
Keung and Jovita plot a scatter diagram of their results.
Explain how they can see the strength of the correlation from their scatter diagram.

parts.label: (e)
parts.text:
Keung and Jovita’s friend says that their results show that the difference in physical activity
level is affecting attention level.
Explain why they cannot draw this conclusion from their research.

text: Keung and Jovita are planning a correlational study to investigate the relationship between a
person’s physical activity level and their attention level. They each make a different prediction
about their results.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Suggest how one extraneous variable could affect Dr Wilson’s study.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text:
Dr Wilson is using a volunteer sample of students from his university.
Suggest how he could recruit his sample.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text: Suggest one advantage of using a volunteer sample compared to an opportunity sample.

parts.label: (iii)
parts.text:
Suggest one disadvantage of using a volunteer sample compared to an opportunity
sample.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
One reason why Dr Wilson cannot generalise the results from his study is his sampling
technique.
State one reason why he should not generalise the results from his students to all internet
users, other than his sampling technique.

Question 10 appears on Page 10.
Section C
Answer all questions in this section.

text: Dr Wilson is conducting an experiment on memory for complex, coloured shapes. He is using
students for his sample. Dr Wilson intends to generalise his results widely, to understand how well
internet users remember visual stimuli.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Describe how Dr Birkin could conduct an observational study of children to investigate their
imaginary play behaviour.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Identify one practical weakness/limitation with the procedure you have described in your
answer to part (a) and suggest how your study might be done differently to overcome the
problem.
Do not refer to ethics or sampling in your answer.
